fichas.title: Optimal Orientation of Rooms
fichas.summary: A compass-oriented diagram groups domestic rooms according to preferred orientation. It associates service and storage rooms with the north; communal rooms with the west; living and dining rooms with the south; and bedrooms and other rooms with the east. The diagram also notes ventilation for the drying room.
uses: Arrange rooms in relation to compass direction and their preferred environmental qualities.

fichas.title: Orientation and Site Planning for Detached Housing
fichas.summary: Detached and semi-detached houses with boundary walls can be oriented in four (three) compass directions, at the cost of higher development costs and lower urban-planning density (p. 137). Plots are generally narrow and long to reduce road frontage. For plots south of a road, the text recommends placing entrance-side rooms toward the north and living rooms and bedrooms away from the road, with sunshine and a garden outlook. For plots north of a road, siting the house toward the back of the plot can make use of a sunny front garden. For plots east or west of a north–south road, it recommends placing the garden and living rooms on the wind-protected east side, with the house toward the north of the plot, to avoid neighbouring buildings shading the low eastern sun.
uses: Orient the house and rooms to address compass direction, road position, sunlight, wind protection, privacy, and garden access.

fichas.title: Orientation and Layout of Housing in Blocks
fichas.summary: In block and row housing, most homes or flats face two opposing directions with different qualities of view, lighting, and noise. Traditional block development may use varied flat layouts and orientations to compensate for unfavourable lighting. Alongside functionally neutral corridor plans, open, flowing, and flexible plans are also proposed. The quality of block structures can be enhanced by views through streets and inner courtyards. An east–west arrangement of rows with green areas between them can provide more uniform lighting and orientation for many flats, at the cost of public space and with a risk of visual monotony.
uses: Plan housing layouts and row orientation to address lighting, views, and noise.

fichas.title: Relation of House to Plot
fichas.summary: The diagrams identify plot-planning considerations including expansiveness or closeness, exposure and shadowing, access, neighbouring buildings, topography, and vegetation. They illustrate house placement in relation to the road and distinguish front and back gardens.
uses: Assess site conditions and arrange the house, access, and gardens in relation to the road and neighbouring properties.
